_review.scope: BRIEF-10.md Part 5 only: 78 wasteland street/city/slums/industry files, summer and winter. Other art is comparison material, not part of the verdict.
_review.calibration: Good enough to ship beside the approved art. Larger deliberate pixel clusters and modest weathering are acceptable when silhouettes, material planes and openings remain readable at 1x. Cosmetic imperfections alone are not failures.

general_findings: Every required Part 5 file is present and has the specified dimensions. All 76 sprites have only binary alpha, occupy the bottom rows (last opaque row is height-2), and are centred within 0.5px. Both bases are opaque.
No blur or blended-alpha edge was found. At 8x, contours remain discrete pixel steps; no visible light fringe/halo was found on the transparency backing or planted ground.
Rust, tan concrete and grey salvage remain compatible with the approved wasteland markers. Broad planes improve native readability; no blanket rejection based on low colour count or local weathering.

No near-duplicate pair within the seasonal building sets was found: rooflines, heights, additions and functions remain distinguishable. Summer/winter counterparts are intentionally the same architecture. Repeated draws of a variant in the random composite are not duplicate assets.
Top surfaces and left-facing planes retain the light emphasis; no sprite has a concrete reversed-light defect. All winter sprites have visible roof/ledge snow and retain the summer structure.

The winter base is the sole remaining failure: the original blankness is gone, but conspicuous recurring diagonal slush bands and pools violate the calm seamless-ground requirement. This is repetition, not a hard wrap-edge seam.

fail.name: wasteland-street@winter-base
fail.problems: The winter is no longer blank, and the wrap joins are clean, but the 3x3 field now exposes a strong 288px repeat: the broad diagonal slush streaks cross into repeated X/chevron bands, and the same large dark pools near source positions (210,70) and (45,195) recur in obvious rows. This remains visible at 1x, 4x and in the sparse planted districts, where the ground competes with buildings. Reduce the value contrast of the large pools and swipes, break up the long crossing diagonals, and redistribute smaller, irregular exposed-rubble/slush patches so no single patch or directional band identifies the tile. Keep the buried cracks, restrained snow texture and seamless edges; do not return to the previous blank blue-grey field.
